teams.heading: Jake White dreams of Fiji hosting Ireland in a Suva Test match
teams.body: In an interview with The42 this week, Jake White sets out a bigger ambition for Fiji: a Test in Suva against Ireland would be the best of all. It is a notable hope, since Fiji's Nations Championship home games this summer were played on UK soil, their national stadium not considered of a suitable standard for regular Tests. White, who beat Warren Gatland and Shaun Edwards to the job last month, is working towards a more consistent side for next year's World Cup in Australia.

lead.why: The Suva ambition is a fresh angle from the White interview, and the move-to-Fiji and Higgins stories have already run.

teams.heading: Fans rage as ITV runs split-screen adverts during England's Japan rout
teams.body: Split-screen adverts during ITV's coverage of Saturday's England v Japan game drew complaints on X, with viewers saying the breaks spoiled the experience. "This is not America." one wrote, while another objected to "watching rugby union, not the NFL." One viewer said the broadcaster cut away from a TMO check for an advert, and others defended the ads, arguing that rugby's finances left it in no position to be choosy.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont inspires France to end South Africa run with 21-19 win
teams.body: France ended a five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France on Friday, winning 21-19 after three first-half tries from Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey. Antoine Dupont, named player of the match, gathered the ball that sealed it after Bielle-Biarrey's huge defensive tackle forced a loose ball late on. Manie Libbok had missed the conversion to Malcolm Marx's try that would have levelled the game. The win leaves France six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings before Argentina next Saturday.

lead.why: A fresh match report on France's 21-19 win over South Africa, the strongest new item and not the Marchand story already run.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi says Italy dominated first half but failed to convert pressure
teams.body: Argentina coach Felipe Contepomi conceded after the Genoa win that Italy had the better of possession and territory in the first half, but said matches like this are decided by who turns control into points. Monty Ioane's fourth-minute try gave the Azzurri the early lead, yet they could not convert sustained pressure, and Bautista Bernasconi's maul try before the break put Argentina ahead 7-5 at half-time. Italy's yellow cards for Joel Sclavi and Efrain Elias proved costly in the second half, and Argentina went on to win 19-14.

teams.heading: Tuipulotu says Scotland are set on bouncing back from All Blacks defeat
teams.body: Scotland's next step after a 21-43 defeat by New Zealand at Murrayfield comes against Australia on Sunday, and captain Sione Tuipulotu says the footage makes hard viewing. Tuipulotu, who was born and raised in Melbourne, says the side missed big chances and let themselves down in certain areas. "Our minds are firmly set on bouncing back after last week." He expects the Wallabies to arrive wounded after their beating by England at Twickenham, and says his own history with Australia adds a little fire.

lead.why: It is the freshest new Scotland-focused item in the shortlist, with captain quotes on how the side is responding to the New Zealand defeat.

teams.heading: Wales end 73-year All Blacks drought with 35-28 win in Cardiff
teams.body: Wales were given little chance, and the decisive stretch came in the final quarter, when the defence led by James Botham, Jac Morgan and Dafydd Jenkins held New Zealand out after New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai's try had pulled the visitors within seven. Tomos Williams scored one of five Welsh tries and had a hand in all of them, with hooker Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit also crossing. Sections of the New Zealand media had belittled Welsh rugby beforehand.

lead.why: A fresh result report that ends a 73-year wait and a 34-match losing run, and the strongest new item on the shortlist.

teams.body: England scored seven tries in a 45-22 rout at Twickenham last weekend, and the Wallabies were taken apart in a performance the BBC described as listless. The defeat leaves Australia having lost three of their four Nations Championship matches and out of contention for the inaugural final. Sunday's visit to Murrayfield now carries the threat of a fourth straight Test defeat, against a Scotland side also seeking to bounce back from their defeat by New Zealand.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns co-captained Japan in Saturday's 78-15 defeat to England at Twickenham
teams.body: Warner Dearns took a roundabout route to the Japan side. He was 14 when his father Grant took a strength and conditioning job with NEC Green Rockets, moving the family from New Zealand's North Island to a satellite city outside Tokyo, and he initially did not want to go. Kashiwa Senior High School turned him into a monster prospect, and he debuted for Japan in November 2021 at 19. This year he spent a sabbatical at the Hurricanes, helping Wellington to their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

teams.heading: All Blacks beaten 35-28 in Cardiff as Wales end 73-year wait
teams.body: Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 at the Principality Stadium, with Tomos Williams and Dewi Lake scoring inside the first six minutes. New Zealand levelled 21-21 at half-time, but Peter Lakai's try only pulled one back. A defence led by James Botham, Jac Morgan and Dafydd Jenkins held the All Blacks up three times over the line in the final quarter. The win ends Wales' 34-match losing run against New Zealand, dating back to 1953.

lead.why: A fresh result from Saturday's Test that the All Blacks lost, and the most talked-about New Zealand story in today's coverage.

teams.heading: Ruan Nortjé rejects card excuse for Springboks' Paris defeat to France
teams.body: Friday's 21-19 loss in Paris left Ruan Nortjé unwilling to blame Jasper Wiese's red card or Lood de Jager's yellow, noting France played 30 minutes a man down too. "We can't put the blame on that at all," he said. The bigger worry is the route to the Nations Championship final: South Africa no longer control it and must rely on other results, starting with Ireland. "It's going to be all about looking at what we did wrong," Nortjé added.

lead.why: A fresh player quote that rejects the card excuse and spells out what the defeat does to South Africa's route to the final, which the other items don't cover.
